title: "Hands-On: History Archaeology"
---

# Hands-on: history archaeology

A test now allows only three retries. Who introduced that limit, and did a later edit change it? In this lab you will build a small `desk-api` history and answer from Git evidence. You need Git and a POSIX shell. The lab creates a fresh directory under the system temporary directory; it does not touch an existing repository or require a network connection.

## Create the evidence

Run the whole block in a terminal. `mktemp -d` prints a new directory name; the assignment saves it for the rest of the block. The identity settings apply only to this practice repository.

```sh
lab_dir=$(mktemp -d)
printf 'Lab directory: %s\n' "$lab_dir"
cd "$lab_dir" || exit 1
git init -q
git config user.name 'Lab Author'
git config user.email 'lab@example.test'
cat > retry.py <<'PY'
def retry_limit():
    return 5
PY
git add retry.py
git commit -q -m 'Add retry limit'
cat > retry.py <<'PY'
def retry_limit():
    return 3
PY
git add retry.py
GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Mina Example' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='mina@example.test' \
  git commit -q -m 'Limit retries to reduce load'
git mv retry.py policy.py
git commit -q -m 'Rename retry policy'
printf '\n# Used by the request handler.\n' >> policy.py
git add policy.py
git commit -q -m 'Document policy use'
```

Commit IDs and dates will vary. The author on the limit change is Mina; the local committer is Lab Author. This distinction matters when reporting attribution.

## Investigate before looking at the answers

1. Use `git blame` to find the commit and author for `return 3` in `policy.py`. Inspect that commit's message and patch. What changed, and what reason does the message give?
2. Use `git log -S` to find changes in the number of occurrences of `return 3`. Try both with and without `--follow` and the current path. Why can the results differ?
3. Use `git log --follow -- policy.py` to reconstruct the file's history. Did the documentation commit alter the limit? Verify rather than inferring from the subject.
4. Compare `git show --stat` with `git show` for the limit change. Which view supplies enough evidence to determine the old value?

## One investigation

```sh
git blame -L 2,2 -- policy.py
# Replace LIMIT_COMMIT with the ID printed by blame.
git show LIMIT_COMMIT
git log --oneline -S 'return 3' -- policy.py
git log --oneline --follow -S 'return 3' -- policy.py
git log --oneline --follow -- policy.py
git show HEAD -- policy.py
```

Blame attributes line 2 to Mina's limit commit. Its patch changes `return 5` to `return 3`; its message says the purpose was to reduce load. This is evidence of the stated intent, not independent proof of the load reduction. The last commit adds a comment and leaves the limit unchanged, as its patch shows.

Without `--follow`, the path-limited pickaxe walk stops at the current name and can report the rename as an addition of the string at that path. With `--follow`, Git follows the detected rename backward and finds the earlier change that introduced `return 3`. `--follow` is limited to a single path and depends on rename detection; large rewrites or complicated histories may defeat it. Investigate the patch and both names when results look surprising. `-S` detects changes in the number of occurrences; use `-G` when a matching line changed but the count stayed the same.

The `--stat` view summarizes the file and line counts. The patch from plain `git show LIMIT_COMMIT` contains the old and new values. `git show LIMIT_COMMIT:retry.py` also prints the saved file at that revision, but on its own does not show the previous value.

## Take it further

Change the comment in a new commit, then repeat `git blame -L 2,2 -- policy.py`. Does the author of the unchanged line change? Add a second occurrence of `return 3` in a new commit and run the pickaxe query again. Explain why it now finds another commit. When finished, leave the lab directory with `cd`; remove the printed temporary directory only if you no longer need it.

Further reference: [Git blame](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-blame), [Git log and pickaxe](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log), and [Git diff options](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff).
